member.name: T:Physics.Wasm.PhysicsBridge
member.summary:
The entire JS-facing surface of the physics simulation. Mirrors 's own "opaque handles + primitives only" design one level further out: every handle here is a plain int id minted by this class (never a raw Bepu or Physics handle value), and every shape/pose parameter is individual doubles rather than a struct, because that's what the built-in JSExport marshaler understands without any custom interop glue.
Intended caller: physics.worker.ts, once per fixed-timestep tick: const packed = PhysicsBridge.Step(dt); // Float64Array, 8 doubles per body const events = PhysicsBridge.GetLastOverlapEvents(); // Int32Array, 3 ints per event
Not yet ported (same pattern, just not wired up - see BUILD.md "Extending the bridge"): AddConvexHullShape, AddTriangleMeshShape, SweepProjectile, SweepSphereCast. Their PhysicsWorld methods take ReadOnlySpan<Vector3>, which needs an explicit [JSMarshalAs<JSType.Array<JSType.Number>>] double[] parameter instead - flatten [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1,...] on the JS side and rebuild the span here, same as everything below already does for single vectors/quaternions.

member.name: M:Physics.Wasm.PhysicsBridge.Step(System.Double)
member.summary: Advances the simulation and returns every dynamic/kinematic body's fresh pose as a flat buffer: [bodyId, posX, posY, posZ, quatX, quatY, quatZ, quatW] repeated once per body currently registered, in unspecified order. Call GetLastOverlapEvents() immediately after to read this same step's Entered/Exited transitions.

member.name: M:Physics.Wasm.PhysicsBridge.GetLastOverlapEvents
member.summary: Flat buffer from the most recent Step(): [ownerIdA, ownerIdB, entered(0/1)] per event.
